Pairing a host
On the host selection screen pick a computer from the list or choose “Add host”. For an unpaired host MoonWaker asks for the six-digit code shown by Host Control on the computer and pairs both the Gateway and streaming.

Profiles and PIN
After choosing a host you see the Windows profiles of that computer. A PIN-protected profile asks for its code first. Child profiles have a daily time limit and allowed hours; a parent changes them after entering the parent PIN.

Diagnostics

When the gyro turns the camera. Hold to enable: only while the button is held (e.g. L2 while aiming down sights). Hold to disable: always, the button lets you reposition the controller without turning the camera. Toggle: the button switches it on and off.

A multiplier for turning left and right. 1.0 = like the controller: the camera turns as far as the controller, once the gearing is set. Above 1.0 a smaller hand movement turns the camera the same amount.
A multiplier for tilting up and down. 1.0 = like the controller. Set it apart from horizontal if vertical aiming feels too fast or too slow.
Reverses the direction of this axis. Change it if the camera moves the opposite way to the controller.
Player space turns around the vertical however you hold the controller. Yaw uses the controller\'s own axis; roll tilts it like a steering wheel.

The gyro stops while you move the right stick, so the stick alone turns the camera. Turn it on if the stick and the gyro fight each other.
Fast turns move the camera further, so slow aiming stays precise and a quick turn reaches far. Standard doubles the speed from 75°/s. When on, the camera no longer turns 1:1 with the controller.
Raise it if small turns barely move the camera while large ones are fine; 2.0 undoes a squared stick response. 1.0 = no change.
Game turn speed at full stick

How fast the game turns the camera with the right stick pushed all the way, in °/s. With sensitivity 1.0 the camera then turns exactly as far as the controller. To set it: while aiming, turn the controller a quarter turn (90°) at a calm pace; the camera should turn 90° too. If it turns less, lower the value; if it turns more, raise it. Turn off aim and turn acceleration in the game, and match the game stick deadzone and curve below, or 1:1 will not hold.

How much mouse movement (counts) the game needs for one full camera turn, like “Pixels per 360°” in Steam Input. With sensitivity 1.0 the camera then turns exactly as far as the controller. To set it: while aiming, turn the controller a quarter turn (90°); the camera should turn 90° too. If it turns less, raise the value; if it turns more, lower it. Changing the mouse sensitivity in the game changes this number; turn mouse acceleration off in the game.
On: the TV turns controller rotation into aiming and the game gets no motion. Off: the game gets the controller\'s motion sensors as before, only for games with their own gyro support.
